extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of legacy CCR surface impoundments, environmental consultants, state/tribal regulators, and EPA compliance staff
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and evaluation criteria for certifying closure, groundwater monitoring, design and structural assessments, and related documentation for legacy coal combustion residual (CCR) surface impoundments under the EPA final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification: two consecutive sampling events below GWPS
rubrics_metrics.description: The facility must have groundwater monitoring data demonstrating that the concentrations of each Appendix IV constituent do not exceed the relevant groundwater protection standard, which would be either the MCL or background concentration, for two consecutive sampling events, consistent with §257.95(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA anticipates the two consecutive sampling events will result in one sample being taken during the dry season and one in the wet season to capture groundwater fluctuations. The last sample used to demonstrate no Appendix IV constituent exceeds the GWPS must have been collected no earlier than one year prior to the initiation of closure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific validity and detectability of supporting data
rubrics_metrics.description: Data supporting a closure certification must be scientifically valid and must credibly support a determination that the monitoring system would reliably detect any releases from the impoundment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA does not require that the monitoring system used to produce legacy data complied with all part 257 monitoring requirements at the time monitoring was conducted, but the data must be scientifically valid. EPA requires the owner/operator to demonstrate the monitoring system met a subset of performance standards (see related item).

rubrics_metrics.name: Groundwater monitoring system performance criteria (six specific criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: The facility must demonstrate that the groundwater monitoring system met a subset of the performance standards found in §§257.91(a)-(e), 257.93(a)-(d), and 257.93(i). Specifically, the monitoring system must:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (1) Accurately represent background water quality unaffected by a CCR unit; (2) Accurately represent the quality of water passing the waste boundary of the unit; (3) Be capable of detecting contamination in the uppermost aquifer; (4) Monitor all potential contaminant pathways; (5) Establish groundwater background concentrations for Appendix IV constituents and compare samples to those background concentrations; and (6) Utilize wells that are (a) cased and maintained to protect borehole integrity, (b) screened/perforated and packed with gravel or sand where necessary to enable sampling, and (c) sealed between borehole and casing to prevent contamination of sample and groundwater.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to obtain monitoring data by installing compliant monitoring system
rubrics_metrics.description: If a facility removed CCR before the rule's effective date but lacks monitoring data (or has monitoring that does not meet the criteria), the facility may install a groundwater monitoring system and initiate monitoring in accordance with §§257.90–257.95 to obtain the information necessary to support a closure certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner/operator must prepare a notification of intent to certify closure by the effective date, place it in the operating record, post it on the CCR website, and submit notification to EPA/State/Tribal Authority. If no statistically significant level (SSL) above the GWPS is detected for all Appendix IV constituents in at least the first two consecutive sampling events (consistent with §257.95(e)), the facility may complete the closure certification and document compliance with §257.102(c). Deadline: completion of certification of closure by removal for these units is no later than 42 months after the effective date of the final rule; the monitoring/analysis schedule follows the rule's timelines (e.g., develop network, sampling and analysis plan, collect baseline samples, combined detection/assessment monitoring).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and public record requirements for certification
rubrics_metrics.description: When pursuing closure by removal certification, the owner/operator must document and notify relevant parties and make records public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare and place a notification of intent to certify closure in the operating record, post the notice on the facility CCR website, and submit a notification to EPA or the State/Tribal Authority. Upon completion of the closure certification, place the certification in the operating record, submit a notification to State/Tribal Authority, and post the certification documentation on the public CCR website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequence if monitoring detects SSL above GWPS (corrective action applicability and timelines)
rubrics_metrics.description: If groundwater monitoring detects an SSL above the established GWPS of any Appendix IV constituent, the legacy CCR surface impoundment becomes subject to corrective action requirements in §§257.96–257.98 and is no longer eligible to certify closure by removal under this provision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner/operator must prepare the applicability report no later than six months from date of receiving the laboratory analysis documenting the SSL; install the permanent marker no later than eight months from that date; comply with CCRMU requirements (with compliance deadlines delayed by number of months between publication and receipt of lab analysis documenting exceedance). If a CCRMU is discovered onsite, prepare a fugitive dust plan no later than 6 months after completion of the FER. For units unable to certify, corrective action may be completed during a post-closure care period and owners/operators may elect to defer closure to permitting if criteria in Unit III.B.2.g.iii are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of location restrictions and liner design criteria (not required for legacy units)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is not applying the location restrictions (§§257.60–257.64) or the liner design criteria (e.g., documentation of composite liners under §257.71(a)(1)) to legacy CCR surface impoundments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: legacy impoundments are not operational, largely unlined, and will be required to close, so the location and liner criteria intended for operational safety are not appropriate or would be redundant. EPA expects information useful for corrective action or closure that would be obtained by complying with location/liner rules will be captured by history of construction, closure plan, or groundwater monitoring system development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of structural integrity/design criteria (§257.73) to legacy impoundments
rubrics_metrics.description: Legacy CCR surface impoundments are subject to the existing design criteria requirements in §257.73 to help prevent damages associated with structural failures, including required reports/assessments (history of construction, initial hazard potential classification, initial structural stability assessment, initial safety factor assessment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA finalized application of §257.73 to legacy units but extended compliance deadlines (see individual items below) to address commenter concerns about contractor availability, seasonality, historical documentation access, and quality assurance/quality control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent identification marker requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators (except incised CCR surface impoundments) must install a permanent identification marker at least six feet high on or immediately adjacent to the CCR unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marker must display the name of the legacy CCR surface impoundment, the name of the owner/operator of the unit, and the identification number of the CCR unit if assigned by the State. Deadline: no later than two months after the effective date of the final rule (codified as no later than January 8, 2025).

rubrics_metrics.name: History of construction report requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators of legacy CCR surface impoundments meeting size thresholds must compile a history of construction report documenting identifying characteristics, how the unit was used, specifics related to design and construction, and the unit's instrumentation, per §257.73(c)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA intends facilities to provide relevant design and construction information only if factual documentation exists; owners/operators are not expected to generate new information or provide anecdotal or speculative information ('reasonably and readily available'). Place the report in the operating record (§257.105(f)(9)) and update if information changes. Deadline: no later than February 9, 2026 (15 months after effective date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial hazard potential classification assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators (except incised units) must determine the hazard potential classification (low, significant, or high) of the CCR unit and justify the determination in a report certified by a P.E., per §257.73(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No commenters objected to the substance; EPA finalized the requirement and extended the deadline to 18 months after the effective date (no later than May 8, 2026). Subsequent periodic hazard potential classifications are required every five years as described at §257.73(f)(3). The hazard classification informs inflow design flood and EAP triggers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial structural stability assessment and safety factor assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators meeting the size thresholds in §257.73(b) and (c) must conduct initial structural stability and safety factor assessments documenting whether the unit's design, construction, operation, and maintenance are consistent with recognized and generally accepted good engineering practices and whether calculated factors of safety meet minimums in §§257.73(e)(1)(i)-(iv).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted good engineering practices include stable foundations/abutments, adequate slope protection, sufficiently compacted dikes, spillways capable of managing peak discharge events, structurally sound hydraulic structures, and downstream slopes capable of withstanding sudden drawdown. Assessments must be certified by a P.E. Periodic reassessments required every five years (§257.73(f)(3)). EPA finalized the requirement and set the compliance deadline at 18 months after the effective date (no later than May 8, 2026).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency Action Plan (EAP) requirement for high/significant hazard units
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators of legacy CCR surface impoundments identified as high or significant hazard potential must prepare and maintain a written Emergency Action Plan per §257.73(a)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An EAP identifies potential emergency conditions and specifies actions to minimize loss of life and property damage. The EAP relies on the hazard potential classification, history of construction, structural stability, and safety factor assessments. EPA finalized the EAP requirement and aligned the deadline with other design criteria: no later than 18 months after the effective date (no later than May 8, 2026). To prepare the EAP, owners/operators must accurately and comprehensively identify potential failure modes and at-risk developments.
